newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran hard currency revenue seen exceeding budget.
newsitem.headline: Iran hard currency revenue seen exceeding budget.

text.p: Iran's hard currency revenue mainly from crude oil exports was expected to exceed budget forecasts by $2 billion in the current Iranian year, an official was quoted on Sunday as saying.

"The country's hard currency revenue by the end of the year (March 1997) will be $2 billion more than predicted in the budget," Hamid Mirzadeh, head of the state Plan and Budget Organisation, told the daily Iran.
Oil revenue is Iran's main source of hard currency and the government's major source of financing if it is to meet debts which officials put at almost $22 billion.
The budget for the current Iranian year envisages petroleum earnings of $15.99 billion, based on exports of 2.6 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude and an average price of $15.50.
Iran had said its revenue from the export of crude oil, refined oil products and gas liquids in the year which ended on March 19, 1996 was $1.6 billion above that set in the state budget.
OPEC member Iran is the world's third largest oil exporter.
Mirzadeh said Iran posted a trade surplus of more than $5 billion last year, on exports of more than $18 billion and imports of around $12.8 billion.
He said unemployment had slowed in the past decade to 9.2 percent from about 14.2 percent a decade ago.
